description: S4: a plain-text follow-up updates an event that was created from an ICS invite. Same event, new location. Must match rather than create a second entry.

content_parts.text:
You are comparing calendar events to detect duplicates.

**New Event:**
- Title: Design Review
- Start: 2026-09-15T14:00:00
- End: 2026-09-15T15:00:00
- Location: Room 4B (moved from Room 2)
- Description: Note the room change for tomorrow's review.

**Existing Events (same date):**

1. Event ID: event-001
   - Title: Design Review
   - Start: 2026-09-15T14:00:00
   - End: 2026-09-15T15:00:00
   - Location: Room 2
   - Description: Invitation: design review.

2. Event ID: event-002
   - Title: Design Systems Guild
   - Start: 2026-09-15T16:00:00
   - End: 2026-09-15T17:00:00
   - Location: Room 2
   - Description: Monthly guild meeting.

**Question:** Is the new event the same as any of the existing events?

Consider events the same if they refer to the same real-world event, even if:
- Wording is slightly different
- One has more details than the other
- Time changed slightly (updates)

Return the matching Event ID (or null if no match) and brief reasoning.

trace.raw_response_text: {"matched_event_id": "event-001", "reasoning": "The new event has the same title, date, and start/end times as event-001. The location differs (Room 4B vs Room 2), but the new event's description says the room was moved from Room 2, so it is an update to the same Design Review meeting. Event-002 is a different meeting (Design Systems Guild at a different time)."}
